definitions: To change the direction of a sailing boat by turning its bow through the wind.
To attach or fasten something with tacks.
To add something as an extra or an afterthought.
To sew with long, loose stitches; to baste.
examples: The captain decided to tack to port.
He will tack the poster to the wall.
They decided to tack on an extra clause to the contract.
She needs to tack the hem before final sewing.
